subject: Integration devkit & lab boarding — SDK quickstart + env setup
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@pathway.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@pathway.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T15:05:00Z
Subject: Integration devkit & lab boarding — SDK quickstart + env setup

Thanks again for your time today — short recap and an actionable plan so we can kick off the hands-on lab next week. I pulled together a minimal checklist to make the SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript) and the local sample apps run smoothly: 

1) Environment inventory (what we need from Pathway):
   - Hostnames/IPs for any internal dev services you want the sample apps to call (if allowed).
   - Preferred auth model: service account (backend-to-backend) or SSO via SAML/OIDC for dev users.
   - Whether any outbound egress is blocked from your dev network (we can provide an on-prem package if so).

2) Quickstart plan (what Redwood will deliver):
   - Two sample apps (Python Flask + TS Node/Express) showing: 
     * simple text generation flow (sync + streaming),
     * a structured-output example with tool-calling stub (external search connector),
     * embedding generation + an example reranker pipeline (embedding -> cosine search -> rerank).
   - Dockerfiles for local runs and a docker-compose that spins up a lightweight vector store (FAISS local image) + sample data.
   - Auth examples: API key env var, short-lived service token flow, and a SAML/SSO dev hint doc.
   - Routing examples: route by model family (latency vs cost) and a fallback to a cheaper quantized model.
   - Small test harness: smoke tests to validate auth, end-to-end generation, and embedding/reranker outputs.

3) Immediate asks for Pathway (can you send before Tue?):
   - samir@ — SAML metadata (if SSO path), otherwise a test API key for dev sandbox.
   - elena@ — confirmation of any data retention / HIPAA constraints we should model in the lab (redaction requirements, fields to omit).

4) Proposed timeline:
   - Tue: Pathway provides one of the items above.
   - Wed–Thu: Redwood creates repo with sample apps + Docker compose and shares a PR + runbook.
   - Fri: 45–60 minute joint lab (we remote in, walk through local run and smoke tests).

If that looks good I’ll assign Marissa to own the sample repo and Karthik will scope the reranker/embeddings flow. Optional: we can prepare a short annotated recording of the lab.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a PR link and a calendar invite for the joint lab once we have the env item.

—
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
"Making inference predictable."
From: Samir Rao <samir@pathway.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@pathway.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T18:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Integration devkit & lab boarding — SDK quickstart + env setup

Appreciate the detailed plan, Dylan — this is exactly what we need. Couple quick answers: 

- We prefer a service-account backend flow for the lab (dev sandbox will accept a hosted API key for now). I attached our SAML metadata in case we need to show SSO later.
- No egress blocks on our infra for dev environments. We will not provide internal hostnames for the lab; the sample apps can call public test endpoints.
- HIPAA: we are subject to HIPAA for production only. For the dev lab we can use de-identified test data; Elana will share a short note on redaction rules.

Files attached: pathway-saml-metadata.xml, env-inventory.xlsx

Samir
CTO | Pathway.ai
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@pathway.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@pathway.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T20:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Integration devkit & lab boarding — SDK quickstart + env setup

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Pathway's confirmation and attachments. Please see the asks below and turn this into a draft repo + runbook: 

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: create the repo pathway-devkit-samples. Add a top-level README with run instructions (env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENDPOINT). Create Python sample: Flask app + sample script samples/generate_text.py demonstrating streaming and structured-output JSON. Add dockerfile and docker-compose referencing local FAISS image.
- Karthik: implement TS sample (Node/Express) and the reranker example. Provide a minimal reranker pipeline in samples/rerank/ that:
    * generates embeddings via /embeddings,
    * inserts sample vectors into the local FAISS container,
    * performs a cosine search and runs a small prompt-based reranker over the top-K.
- Both: add smoke tests under tests/ that run in the container and assert the generation API returns 200 and that embeddings vectors are non-empty.

Deadline: draft repo + PR by 2027-05-01 EOD so we can iterate before the joint lab. Samir asked for a Fri session but we’ll coordinate after the PR is up.

Let me know if any blockers — I’ll prep the calendar once PR is visible.

Thanks,
Dylan

Subject: Re: Integration devkit & lab boarding — SDK quickstart + env setup

Thanks everyone — confirmed on using de-identified data for the lab. Two small notes: 

- Please avoid storing PHI in any persistent vector store in the sample repo; ephemeral only for the lab is fine. Can you add a code comment and README note about that?
- Could we include a tiny example of a structured-output schema (JSON schema) for a clinical extraction example (e.g., fields: diagnosis, medication, note_confidence) so our engineers can see mapping to downstream systems?

Happy to join the lab — Fri is best for us (PST).

—
Elena Torres
Head of Platform | Pathway.ai
